name: Rangpo
tagline: Gateway town where the Teesta meets the Rangpo
meta_description: Rangpo, Sikkim: the gateway town at about 333 m on NH10 where the Teesta and Rangpo rivers meet. Check post, jeep fares, Maghe Sankranti and onward routes.
summary: Rangpo is the first town in Sikkim on NH10, at about 333 m, where the Rangpo river joins the Teesta. Wikipedia calls it the Gateway to Sikkim: every vehicle stops at the police check post, and foreigners must show documents. The Sevoke to Rangpo railway is not open; completion is targeted for December 2027.
intro: Rangpo is a municipal town shared between Pakyong district in Sikkim and Kalimpong district in West Bengal, on the border formed by the Rangpo river. It is the first town of Sikkim on National Highway 10, which links Siliguri to Gangtok, and Wikipedia says all vehicles entering Sikkim have to stop at the Rangpo police check-post. Foreign tourists must present their documents here.

At about 333 m it is hot and humid in summer and a gateway rather than a destination. Roads branch to Rorathang and Rongli, to Namchi via Namthang and to Kalimpong via Munsoong. Wikipedia lists shared jeeps and SNT buses to Gangtok, Siliguri and NJP, with Bagdogra about 90 km away.

The Teesta and Rangpo meet below the town, and both rivers rise fast in the monsoon from June to September. NH10 can close after landslides, and the Sevoke to Rangpo railway is not open, with completion targeted for December 2027. Check current status before you travel.

story.title: The gateway and the two rivers
story.text: Wikipedia's article on Rangpo says the town lies on the belt of two rivers: the Teesta, coming from the Dikchu, Singtam and Majitar side, and the Rangpo, coming from Rongli, Rorathang and Kumrek. They meet below the town at a spot called Rangpo Doban. The article calls the Teesta the largest river of Sikkim and the Rangpo the third largest, and warns that both become violent between June and September, sometimes flooding the lower town. It also says the Rangpo river separates the Rangpo Forest Village on the West Bengal side from the municipal town on the Sikkim side. That is why the place works as a gateway: the highway enters Sikkim along river valleys, and vehicles must stop at the check post. The town's riverbanks also draw families for the Maghe Sankranti bath in mid-January, when people gather at river confluences.

little_known.fact: Wikipedia says Rangpo averages about 333 m above sea level, and has a sub-tropical climate.
Roads join NH10 at Rangpo from Rorathang via Kumrek, from Namchi via Namthang and from Kalimpong via Munsoong, according to Wikipedia.
Wikipedia says the nearest functioning railway stations are Sivok about 55 km, Siliguri Junction about 75 km and New Jalpaiguri about 87 km. The Rangpo station is under construction.

facts: Oct–Mar; hot and humid in summer
Not needed; foreigners show documents at check post

highlights.title: The check post
highlights.text: All vehicles entering Sikkim stop here, and foreign tourists show documents. Carry photo ID for everyone. Expect a short queue on weekends and holidays.

highlights.title: Where two rivers meet
highlights.text: The Teesta and the Rangpo meet below the town. Both rise quickly in the monsoon, so view from a safe place on the bank and do not go near the edge.

highlights.title: Maghe Sankranti on the riverbank
highlights.text: In mid-January, around the first day of Magh, families come to bathe and share winter foods at river confluences. Visit as a guest and ask before photographing.

highlights.title: Road junction
highlights.text: Roads branch to Rorathang and Rongli, to Namchi and to Kalimpong. Shared jeeps and SNT buses link Rangpo with Gangtok, Siliguri and NJP.

highlights.title: Supplies stop
highlights.text: Banks, ATMs and shops line the highway. Fill water and cash here before heading to Aritar, Rongli or Gangtok.

how_to_reach.text: Shared jeeps run from Gangtok (via Singtam) and from Siliguri to Rangpo all day, roughly ₹150–250 from Gangtok and ₹250–400 from Siliguri. SNT buses also run. Check current status before you travel.
From Gangtok about 40 km and 1.5 to 2 hours by NH10. A reserved small car costs about ₹2,500–3,500 one way. NH10 closes after monsoon slides; the alternative is via Kalimpong and Algarah or Lava.

About 90 km from Bagdogra and 87 km from NJP by Wikipedia's figures, taking 3 to 3.5 hours via Sevoke. Pakyong Airport has no scheduled flights since June 2024. The Sevoke to Rangpo railway is not open.

costs: Reserved small car Rangpo to Aritar
where_to_stay: Rangpo has business hotels and a few budget lodges at roughly ₹1,200–2,200 a room for people stopping overnight, though we do not name individual properties. Most travellers go on to Gangtok, Pakyong or Aritar. Vivanta Sikkim at Pakyong is the comfort option, about 25 km away, and Aritar's lakeside homestays suit a first night before the Silk Route. If your train or flight arrives late, ask us for a check-post-friendly early start.
tips: Keep photo ID accessible for the check post.
Foreigners should carry passports and the Restricted Area Permit confirmation.
In monsoon, check NH10 status before you leave Siliguri.
Do not go near the river edge in or after heavy rain.
Arrive before dark to avoid hill-road fatigue.

experiences.title: Maghe Sankranti on the Rangpo riverbank
experiences.image_query: Maghe Sankranti river bath Nepal Sikkim
experiences.summary: On the first day of Magh, families gather at river confluences to bathe and share winter foods. Rangpo's riverbanks are one of the places where it happens in Pakyong district.
body: Wikipedia describes Maghe Sankranti as a Nepali festival observed on the first day of Magh in the Vikram Sambat calendar, marking the end of the winter solstice period. In Sikkim it is a major festival for Nepali-speaking communities and is usually 14 or 15 January.

The custom is to bathe in a river, ideally at a confluence, and then share foods such as sesame and molasses sweets, boiled yam and sweet potato and ghee. Rangpo sits at the meeting of the Rangpo and the Teesta, which makes the riverbanks a natural place.
Visit as a guest: keep a respectful distance, ask before photographing people, especially bathers, and do not enter water yourself unless invited. Check current status and dates before you travel.

faqs.q: When is Maghe Sankranti?
faqs.a: Usually 14 or 15 January, on the first day of Magh in the Nepali calendar. The exact date can vary by a day. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can visitors take part?
faqs.a: As guests, quietly. Do not bathe or join rituals unless invited. Ask before photographing.

faqs.q: Is it safe near the river?
faqs.a: River levels are low in January, but banks are slippery and crowds are heavy. Keep children close and stay on firm ground.

experiences.title: Teesta and Rangpo confluence viewpoint
experiences.summary: A short stop to see where the Rangpo river meets the Teesta below the town, safely from a bank or bridge, and read the geography of this gateway.
body: Wikipedia says the Teesta, the largest river of Sikkim, and the Rangpo, the third largest, meet below Rangpo at a spot called Rangpo Doban. Stand at a safe bank or bridge and look upstream at each valley.
In winter the rivers run clear and lower. In the monsoon from June to September they rise fast and violent, sometimes flooding the lower town, so do not visit then.
The confluence is also a place of local ritual; Wikipedia notes it is used as a cremation place. Keep a respectful distance and do not photograph rituals.

faqs.q: Which river is larger, the Teesta or the Rangpo?
faqs.a: Wikipedia says the Teesta is the largest river in Sikkim and the Rangpo the third largest.

faqs.q: Is it safe to go close to the water?
faqs.a: No, not in or after rain. Stay on the bank and keep children close.

faqs.q: Is the confluence a tourist sight?
faqs.a: Not formally. It is a short viewpoint stop. Treat it with respect, since it is also used for rituals.

experiences.title: Check post stop and bazaar lunch
experiences.summary: A practical stop: clear the check post, withdraw cash and have a plain lunch in the bazaar before heading up to Gangtok or across to Aritar.
body: Every vehicle entering Sikkim stops at the Rangpo check post, and Wikipedia says foreign tourists must show documents. Keep photo ID and permits ready for everyone, and be patient on weekends.
The bazaar has small eateries serving thali, momos, noodles and fried snacks, and shops for water and snacks. Eat where it is busy.
Refill cash and water here. If you are going to Aritar or Rongli, buy supplies now. Check current status of NH10 before you continue.

faqs.q: What documents do we need at the check post?
faqs.a: Photo ID for all Indian travellers. Foreigners need passports and the Restricted Area Permit confirmation. Carry copies. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long does the check post take?
faqs.a: Usually 5 to 20 minutes, longer on holidays and weekends.

faqs.q: Are there vegetarian options?
faqs.a: Yes, thali, vegetable momos and noodles are common. Say if you avoid onion, garlic or egg.

experiences.title: Rangpo to Aritar scenic drive via Rorathang
experiences.summary: Follow the Rangpo river upstream from the gateway through Rorathang to Rhenock and Aritar, watching the valley narrow and the forest take over.
body: Wikipedia says the Rangpo river comes from the Rongli, Rorathang and Kumrek side. The road from Rangpo follows its valley upstream to Rorathang, about 12 km, then climbs to Rhenock and Aritar.
The drive passes cardamom plots, small villages and the occasional waterfall. In the monsoon the road can have slides, so check current status before you travel.
Stop at Rorathang for tea and at viewpoints your driver knows are safe. The whole route takes about 1.5 to 2 hours to Aritar.

faqs.q: How far is Aritar from Rangpo?
faqs.a: About 30 km by Wikipedia's figure, taking about 1.5 to 2 hours.

faqs.q: Is the road safe?
faqs.a: Usually, but slides can happen after rain. Check current status before you travel and ask your driver.

faqs.q: Is there a shared jeep?
faqs.a: Shared jeeps run to Rorathang and Rhenock, then local vehicles to Aritar. A private car is simpler.

faqs.q: What is Rangpo known for?
faqs.a: Rangpo is known as the Gateway to Sikkim: the first Sikkim town on NH10, with a police check post that all vehicles stop at. It lies where the Rangpo river joins the Teesta, at about 333 m.

faqs.q: Do we need a permit at Rangpo?
faqs.a: Indian nationals need only photo ID. Foreigners must show their passport and the Restricted Area Permit. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is Rangpo from Gangtok?
faqs.a: About 40 km, taking 1.5 to 2 hours on NH10. Landslides after monsoon rain can close the road. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is Rangpo from Bagdogra?
faqs.a: Wikipedia gives about 90 km, taking 3 to 3.5 hours via Sevoke, depending on traffic and road conditions. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there a railway to Rangpo?
faqs.a: Not yet. The Sevoke to Rangpo line is not open, with completion targeted for December 2027. The nearest working stations are Sivok, Siliguri and NJP.

faqs.q: Is Rangpo worth a night?
faqs.a: Usually not. It is hot and a gateway. Most travellers go on to Gangtok, Pakyong or Aritar.

faqs.q: What is the best time to pass through Rangpo?
faqs.a: October to March for comfortable weather. Summers are hot and humid, and the monsoon brings slides and floods.

faqs.q: Is the river safe to visit?
faqs.a: Only from a safe bank in dry weather. Both rivers rise fast in the monsoon. Do not swim.

faqs.q: What is Maghe Sankranti at Rangpo?
faqs.a: A mid-January festival, usually 14 or 15 January, when families bathe at river confluences and share winter foods. Visit as a guest and ask before photographing.
